items.detail: At Hex Fight Series 33 in Melbourne, Thicknesse beat Marvin Malunes with elbows in round one. The official fight registry records a knockout but does not give a reliable elapsed clock time; a database placeholder of 0:00 must not be treated as a stoppage time. He improved to 7-0.

items.label: Wins Hex Fight Series bantamweight championship
items.detail: The round-one knockout of Marvin Malunes occurred in a scheduled Hex bantamweight title bout at Hex Fight Series 33. Thicknesse left with the promotional belt, which he also lists in his UFC questionnaire. This was his final recorded fight before joining the UFC.

items.date: Late Jan. 2025 (about ten days before UFC 312)
items.label: Accepts short-notice UFC debut against Aleksandre Topuria
items.detail: While working a security shift, Thicknesse received an Instagram message from Ilia Topuria's manager about an opportunity to fight Aleksandre Topuria at UFC 312. He consulted coach Joe Lopez and training partner Alexander Volkanovski and accepted about ten days out. The precise day of the initial call is not confirmed.

items.label: PRO LOSS · Aleksandre Topuria · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: Thicknesse made his UFC debut at UFC 312 in Sydney, losing a unanimous decision to Aleksandre Topuria after three complete five-minute rounds. All three judges scored it 30-27 for Topuria. His professional record became 7-1. UFC and Sherdog index the bout as Feb. 8, while some Australian event records list Feb. 9.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog fight record / official UFC result

items.label: Describes full training camp for first UFC return
items.detail: Ahead of fighting Josias Musasa in Perth, Thicknesse said he had a complete camp this time rather than the roughly ten days' notice before facing Topuria. He noted he had already been training consistently when the UFC 312 opportunity arrived, so the first fight was not an untrained 'off the couch' appearance.

items.label: PRO WIN · Josias Musasa · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Ulberg vs. Reyes in Perth, Thicknesse defeated Josias Musasa by unanimous decision, 29-28 on all three judges' cards, after three rounds. His first official UFC victory took him to 8-1 overall and 1-1 in the Octagon. Sherdog and UFC date the bout Sep. 27 while some Australian-local publications use Sep. 28.

items.label: PRO WIN · Vince Morales · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Della Maddalena vs. Prates in Perth, Thicknesse won a competitive three-round unanimous decision over Vince Morales, 29-28 on every official scorecard. His professional record improved to 9-1 and his regular UFC record to 2-1. The date is May 2, 2026, despite a mistaken November 2024 date in one sentence on his UFC athlete Q&A.

items.label: Booked for UFC 333 against undefeated Asaf Chopurov
items.detail: The forthcoming Oct. 24 UFC 333 bantamweight contest with undefeated Asaf Chopurov was reported in September. Thicknesse entered the matchup on consecutive UFC decision wins over Musasa and Morales. This is a confirmed scheduled fight, not a completed result.

items.label: Discusses Chopurov, training with Volkanovski and fight adjustments
items.detail: Thicknesse appeared on the heavywgt MMA podcast for a 19:05 interview discussing the Asaf Chopurov matchup, working with Volkanovski, power-punching mechanics, improving performance late in fights, and his approach to Abu Dhabi. The episode also included discussion of Petr Yan's camp. These are the published interview topics, not proof of a permanent gym move.

items.label: Freestyle Fighting Gym remains listed primary team
items.detail: Sherdog and UFC continue to identify Thicknesse with the Freestyle Fighting Gym/Freestyle MMA team under Joe Lopez. His long-running work with Volkanovski is documented; no reliable source establishes a permanent 2026 departure or a new head coach for UFC 333.

items.detail: Chopurov submitted Adriano Ramos by rear-naked choke at 2:24 in the first round and retained his bantamweight championship. This improved his professional record to 10-0.
items.sourceLabel: UAE Warriors official fighter bout log

items.label: WIN · Reece McLaren · KO (right punch) · R1 1:03
items.detail: At UAE Warriors 72, Chopurov defeated Reece McLaren by ko (right punch), recorded at 1:03 of r1. A single right hand dropped the former ONE Championship title challenger. The finish was Chopurov's second successful title defense and moved him to 11-0, ten finishes, with five by KO/TKO and five by submission. This was an official professional MMA victory.

items.label: Defends UAE Warriors belt for second time
items.detail: At UAE Warriors 72 in Abu Dhabi, Chopurov knocked out Reece McLaren at 1:03 of round one with a right hand. He had now won six times for the promotion and recorded two successful defenses of its 135 lb championship.

items.label: UFC signing confirmed with 11-0 professional record
items.detail: MMA Junkie reported his UFC signing on Sept. 24; Sherdog followed on Sept. 25. His 11-0 professional record included five knockouts/TKOs, five submissions and one decision. The proposed Oct. 24 UFC 333 debut was part of the signing coverage, not an already fought UFC result.

items.label: Discusses early Khabib influence and Abdulmanap training camp
items.detail: In comments reported from Ariel Helwani's interview, Chopurov recalled being inspired by Khabib around age 14–15 and attending a camp in Dagestan with Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. The fighter's recollection confirms a training experience but does not provide its exact date.

items.label: Regular Petr Yan training partner entering UFC debut
items.detail: UFC and MMA Junkie describe Chopurov as one of reigning bantamweight champion Petr Yan's principal training partners. They are scheduled to appear on the same UFC 333 card. The reported relationship does not independently establish a new permanent head coach or gym.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Junkie signing coverage / UFC Oct. 2026 feature

items.label: UFC 333 · bantamweight debut vs. Colby Thicknesse
items.detail: Chopurov (11-0 professional, 0-0 UFC) is scheduled to face Colby Thicknesse (9-1 professional, 2-1 UFC) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi on UFC 333. This is his scheduled UFC debut, and no bout result or individual walkout time exists as of Oct. 21, 2026. Early preliminary coverage is advertised for 10 a.m. Eastern / 9 a.m. Central / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi time.

audit.scope: Comprehensive dated rebuild: all 11 Sherdog professional bouts (11-0; 5 KO/TKO, 5 submissions, 1 decision) with rounds, methods and clocks; 35 individually indexed amateur wins and 1 loss including delayed 2021 IMMAF Junior World gold in Jan. 2022; full 2021–2025 amateur tournament history and 34-1 vs 35-1 discrepancy; first Khabib/Abdulmanap inspiration and Dagestan camp, Sambo 34/Chingiz Allazov multi-gym reports, Petr Yan sparring, canceled Tokarev/McLaren bookings, UAE Warriors bantamweight crown and two defenses, UFC signing and Oct. 24 scheduled debut. items.label: Father enrolls him in boxing for fitness
items.detail: Malkoun has said his father enrolled him in boxing because he was overweight as a teenager. A reported starting age of 16 points to roughly 2011–12, but no precise initial training date is documented.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete questionnaire and biographical coverage

items.label: Develops at Gracie Jiu Jitsu Smeaton Grange
items.detail: Malkoun studied and worked part-time before coach Alex Prates offered him an opportunity to teach MMA classes at the Smeaton Grange gym. The arrangement supported regular training. The exact start date is not established.

items.label: Becomes long-term Robert Whittaker training partner
items.detail: Malkoun has trained extensively alongside former UFC middleweight champion Robert Whittaker in Sydney. This is a documented sparring and training relationship, not evidence that Whittaker is his only coach.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Dean Bradley · KO (punch) · R2 0:43
items.detail: At Superfight MMA 1, Malkoun knocked out Dean Bradley at 0:43 of round two. Recorded as amateur MMA, not professional boxing or professional MMA.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Rhys Savage · Unanimous decision · R3 3:00
items.detail: Malkoun defeated Rhys Savage by unanimous decision after three complete three-minute rounds at Superfight MMA 2. Sherdog indexes two amateur victories; neither belongs in his professional 10-3 total.

items.label: Grant Brechney amateur booking does not occur
items.detail: The planned Urban Fight Night 6 amateur contest was canceled and has no official result.

items.label: Adrian Leaitua booking does not occur
items.detail: An Urban Fight Night 8 middleweight booking against Adrian Leaitua did not take place. It is not his professional debut.

items.label: WIN · Cameron (Cam) Rowston · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: BRACE 47 in Sydney. Defeated Cameron (Cam) Rowston by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Professional MMA debut; moved to 1-0. Rowston later joined the UFC middleweight division.

items.label: BOXING WIN · Matthew Saville · TKO · R2 2:35
items.detail: Malkoun defeated Matthew Saville by second-round TKO (2:35) in an Australian professional heavyweight boxing match. This is separate from his MMA record.

items.label: Scheduled bout with Duke Didier canceled
items.detail: BRACE 53 and the proposed light heavyweight fight against Duke Didier were canceled. No 205-pound professional fight took place.

items.label: WIN · Ryan Heketa · TKO (punches) · R1 1:32
items.detail: Hex Fight Series 17. Defeated Ryan Heketa by tko (punches); official recorded round and clock: R1, 1:32. Professional MMA record improved to 2-0.

items.label: Wins ADCC Asia & Oceania Trials, under 99 kg
items.detail: ADCC's official Tokyo results list Malkoun of Gracie Humaita first in the men's -99 kg bracket, ahead of Zaid Sad Sami and Harry Grech. This won qualification for the world championships; it is not itself an ADCC Worlds title.

items.label: WIN · Christophe Van Dijck (Van Dijk) · TKO (punches) · R2/R3 disputed 3:31
items.detail: Wollongong Wars 7. Defeated Christophe Van Dijck (Van Dijk) by tko (punches); official recorded round and clock: R2/R3 disputed, 3:31. The result and 3:31 time are consistent, but sources disagree on the round: Sherdog lists round three while ESPN, Tapology and the opponent's record list round two. The round remains flagged as disputed pending original event records.

items.label: Withdraws from ADCC World Championships roster
items.detail: FloGrappling reported that Malkoun, although qualified through the Asia/Oceania trials, was no longer in the -99 kg field for the 2019 ADCC Worlds. He should not be credited with competing in that world championship.

items.label: BOXING WIN · Waikato Falefehi · Unanimous decision · 4 rounds
items.detail: Malkoun won a four-round professional heavyweight boxing decision at ANBF Best of the Best. Biographies report an overall professional boxing record of 3-0, but only this bout and his Nov. 2017 Matthew Saville contest could be verified individually here.

items.label: Reported Pan Pacific jiu-jitsu gold medal
items.detail: Biographical accounts credit a 2019 Pan Pacific BJJ gold medal. Tournament bracket, exact date and belt division remain insufficiently documented; it is not counted as a verified ADCC world title.

items.label: WIN · Sebastian Temesi · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: Eternal MMA 48 in Melbourne. Defeated Sebastian Temesi by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Improved to 4-0, his last regional professional MMA fight.

items.label: Signs UFC contract at 4-0
items.detail: Malkoun entered the UFC with four professional wins in Australia, little MMA experience compared with typical prospects, and a reputation as Robert Whittaker's training partner.

items.label: LOSS · Phil Hawes · KO (punches) · R1 0:18
items.detail: UFC 254 in Abu Dhabi. Lost to Phil Hawes by ko (punches); official recorded round and clock: R1, 0:18. An 18-second UFC debut knockout loss, his first defeat in professional MMA.

items.label: Works back from confidence loss after UFC debut
items.detail: Malkoun later described the mental challenge of his UFC debut loss and rebuilding his confidence. This is a fighter interview account, not a documented psychiatric diagnosis or physical injury.

items.label: WIN · Abdul Razak Alhassan · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Whittaker vs. Gastelum. Defeated Abdul Razak Alhassan by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. His first UFC win, using sustained wrestling over three rounds.

items.label: First AJ Dobson booking shifts from UFC 270
items.detail: The Jan. 22 AJ Dobson pairing at UFC 270 was rescheduled; the same fighters met on Feb. 12 at UFC 271. No result is assigned to the uncompleted original booking.

items.label: WIN · A.J. Dobson · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC 271 in Houston. Defeated A.J. Dobson by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Second consecutive UFC win; professional record reached 6-1.

items.label: LOSS · Brendan Allen · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC 275 in Singapore. Lost to Brendan Allen by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. His only professional decision loss as of October 2026. He later said he disagreed with the judges, but the Allen victory is official. Event dates differ by source/time zone.

items.label: WIN · Nick Maximov · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Grasso vs. Araujo. Defeated Nick Maximov by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Wrestling-heavy unanimous decision, professional record 7-2.

items.label: Aliaskhab Khizriev and Robert Bryczek bookings fall through
items.detail: The Sep. 23 UFC card initially advertised Aliaskhab Khizriev vs Malkoun. Khizriev withdrew, Robert Bryczek was booked and then withdrew, leaving Cody Brundage as the actual opponent. Neither earlier bout happened.
items.sourceLabel: UFC announcement and Tapology canceled matches

items.label: Talks about Whittaker and frustration with Brendan Allen result
items.detail: In a gym interview published Sep. 22, Malkoun discussed his partnership with Whittaker and his belief that he should have received the Allen decision. His opinion does not alter that official result.

items.label: LOSS · Cody Brundage · Disqualification (illegal back-of-head elbow) · R1 4:15
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Fiziev vs. Gamrot. Lost to Cody Brundage by disqualification (illegal back-of-head elbow); official recorded round and clock: R1, 4:15. Referee Mark Smith stopped the fight after a strike to the back of Brundage's head while he was on the mat; Brundage could not continue after medical assessment. Malkoun lost by DQ, not KO or no contest.

items.label: WIN · Andre Petroski · TKO (body soccer kick and strikes) · R2 0:39
items.detail: UFC Atlantic City: Blanchfield vs. Fiorot. Defeated Andre Petroski by tko (body soccer kick and strikes); official recorded round and clock: R2, 0:39. Official fight records use a soccer kick to the body and follow-up strikes. A kick to the body of a grounded opponent is legal in MMA.

items.label: Serious back injury stalls career
items.detail: Malkoun said he developed persistent back problems after the Petroski win and repeatedly aggravated the issue by trying to train and return too early. Exact diagnosis or surgery is not publicly established.

items.label: Withdraws from scheduled Rodolfo Vieira fight
items.detail: The scheduled Feb. 15, 2025 matchup with Rodolfo Vieira was canceled after Malkoun's injury setback. Andre Petroski replaced Malkoun and fought Vieira instead. He did not compete on the card.

items.label: Almost 22-month layoff during back recovery
items.detail: Malkoun did not fight between Mar. 30, 2024 and Jan. 31, 2026. The interval was about 22 months; his described back injury and recovery were central to the absence. No anti-doping penalty is documented as the cause.

items.label: Discusses impatience, injury setbacks and return
items.detail: Ahead of UFC 325, Malkoun acknowledged that attempting a premature comeback had worsened the injury, and said he had questioned when he would be able to compete again.

items.label: WIN · Torrez Finney · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC 325 in Sydney. Defeated Torrez Finney by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Official scorecards: 30-27, 30-26, 30-26. Return after nearly 22 months away; U.S. broadcast fight date Jan. 31, Australia local date Feb. 1.

items.label: Gerald Meerschaert misses weight by four pounds
items.detail: Meerschaert weighed 190 pounds versus the 186-pound non-title middleweight allowance, while Malkoun weighed 186. The fight proceeded as a 190-pound catchweight bout, with Meerschaert forfeiting 30% of his purse. This is not a Malkoun weight miss.

items.label: WIN · Gerald Meerschaert · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC Perth: Della Maddalena vs. Prates. Defeated Gerald Meerschaert by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Three 29-28 scorecards for Malkoun; he improved to 10-3 overall and 6-3 UFC. Catchweight bout was due to Meerschaert's miss.

items.label: Says Perth performance was below his standards
items.detail: After the decision against Meerschaert, Malkoun publicly expressed disappointment with his own performance despite the win. The official scorecards remained 29-28 on all three cards.

items.label: Smeaton Grange and PMA Super Martial Arts team entries
items.detail: Tapology and ESPN identify Gracie Jiu-Jitsu Smeaton Grange; Sherdog lists PMA Super Martial Arts. Without dated statements establishing a transfer, these affiliations should not be turned into a claimed 2026 permanent gym switch. His Whittaker training partnership is well documented.

items.label: Comments on Vagaev, back recovery and Whittaker sparring
items.detail: In a Fox Sports Australia interview, Malkoun said he was comfortable with Vagaev's wrestling threat, and reported feeling physically better than he had for several years after the back problems. Fox also reports that Malkoun has worked training NRL players for the Penrith Panthers and Canterbury Bulldogs. Malkoun said Whittaker was now much bigger as a sparring partner.
items.sourceLabel: Fox Sports Australia fight-week interview, Oct. 21, 2026

items.label: WIN · Michel Pereira · decision

items.label: Early win streak leads into first major title
items.detail: Vagaev's early professional run, including the Pereira win, carried him into a 2017 World Fighting Championship Akhmat title and established the wrestling-heavy style that later translated to ACA championship success.

items.label: Wins first six professional fights
items.detail: Vagaev opened his professional career with six straight wins. The run included a 2016 decision over future UFC contender Michel Pereira and led into his first major championship in 2017.

items.label: Rebuilds from 0-1 into UFC prospect
items.detail: After losing his debut, Oki put together the regional run that eventually produced two Atomic lightweight titles and a Contender Series opportunity. The stretch reframed his career from an 0-1 start into a UFC-level prospect.

items.label: Works at Domino's and coaches children/private lessons
items.detail: Before the UFC, Oki worked at Domino's Pizza while also coaching kids' classes and giving private lessons at his gym. It is useful context for the regional phase before fighting became his full-time career.

items.label: Valon Team develops MMA around striking-first style

items.label: Trains in Paris alongside Imavov, Saint Denis and Gomis
items.detail: For his Paris camp, Oki trained alongside Nassourdine Imavov, Benoit Saint Denis and William Gomis. The camp gave him regular work with several UFC-level teammates rather than preparing in isolation.

items.label: Starts MMA after watching Anderson Silva
items.detail: Santos began training in 2011 after watching a replay of an Anderson Silva fight. Seeing Silva climb the Octagon and celebrate made Santos want to experience that moment himself. Before fighting, he lived in the countryside and worked in the field; he later accumulated 10 amateur MMA fights and 10 Muay Thai wins.

items.label: 10 amateur MMA fights and 10 Muay Thai wins
items.detail: Before his professional MMA run, Santos accumulated 10 amateur MMA fights and 10 Muay Thai wins. The UFC lists him with a black grade in Muay Thai and a purple belt in jiu-jitsu.

items.detail: Santos trains at Chute Boxe Diego Lima, where his training room has included Charles Oliveira and Allan Nascimento. He describes the aggressive, pressure-heavy approach as part of the Chute Boxe identity.

items.label: Nearly two-year gap between UFC appearances
items.detail: Santos did not compete between his June 2023 win over Johnny Munoz Jr. and his May 2025 return against Jeong Yeong Lee. I have not found a reliable public source identifying one specific injury as the cause, so the timeline records the inactivity without assigning a reason.

items.label: Trains alongside Charles Oliveira and Allan Nascimento

items.label: Training injury forces Fury FC withdrawal
items.detail: While rolling with a heavier partner during a trip to Glory MMA, Steele suffered a joint injury after a reckless transition and was forced out of Fury FC 60. The injury interrupted his pre-UFC grappling/MMA development before he later returned and resumed his rise.

items.label: 2-0 amateur MMA run with Fury FC title
items.detail: Before turning professional, Steele went 2-0 as an amateur with two knockouts and won the Fury FC amateur welterweight championship, adding actual MMA competition to his much deeper grappling résumé.

items.label: Relocates to Las Vegas to build full MMA game
items.detail: Steele moved to Las Vegas and deliberately spent time settling into a full MMA training environment before taking his next fight. The move marked the shift from elite grappler who fought MMA into a fighter building the complete striking-and-grappling game at Syndicate MMA.

items.label: Roughly 200 grappling matches before pro MMA debut
items.detail: By the time Steele approached his professional MMA debut, UFC Fight Pass estimated that he had already accumulated roughly 200 grappling matches. That volume explains why his submission game was far more developed than a normal 0-0 MMA prospect.

items.label: Wins over Andy Varela, Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani and Phil Rowe
items.detail: Steele continued competing in professional grappling while building his MMA career, with wins over Andy Varela, Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani and UFC veteran Phil Rowe among the results listed on his UFC profile.

items.label: Follows brother from judo to boxing to MMA
items.detail: Gugnon says he began by following his brother to judo, then followed him into boxing and finally into MMA around age 15. That progression gave him a mixed striking/grappling foundation before his pro career.

items.label: Ares run becomes career turning point
items.detail: Gugnon has described his first Ares appearance as the point where the French audience really began to notice him. His Ares run became the bridge from a 4-2 record to the finishing streak that brought him to the UFC.

items.label: Six straight finishes rebuild career after 4-2 start
items.detail: After a 4-2 start that included losses to Mark Ewen and Samvel Vardanyan, Gugnon put together a six-fight finishing streak to reach 10-2. The run included four knockouts/TKOs and two rear-naked chokes and carried him into the UFC.

items.label: Runs an e-commerce business and works nightclub security
items.detail: Gugnon says he did not pursue higher education, instead launching an e-commerce business after high school while also working nightclub security. He later described the UFC as the start of his real career.

items.label: Judo and boxing lead into BJJ, Luta Livre and MMA
items.detail: Gugnon followed his brother into the gym, starting with judo and later boxing before moving into MMA around age 15. He now holds purple belts in BJJ and Luta Livre and is a national Pancrase champion.

items.label: Starts fighting after witnessing domestic violence
items.detail: Lucindo says witnessing domestic violence in her family pushed her toward training, with fighting becoming a path toward a better life for her family.

items.label: Multiple MMA and jiu-jitsu titles
items.detail: Before the UFC, Lucindo held regional MMA belts and won Brazilian and state-level jiu-jitsu honors.

items.label: UFC debut vs. Yazmin Jauregui
items.detail: Lucindo lost a unanimous decision in her UFC debut, then began a four-fight UFC winning streak.

items.label: Positive anti-doping sample
items.detail: Lucindo tested positive for mesterolone from a September 24, 2025 out-of-competition sample. CSAD found no evidence of intentional use, and her team provided documentation showing she had obtained compounded supplements from a Brazilian pharmacy that could have been contaminated. She was removed from her December 2025 booking during the investigation.

items.label: Nine-month suspension
items.detail: CSAD imposed a nine-month period of ineligibility beginning September 24, 2025 and ending June 24, 2026. CSAD reduced the potential sanction after finding Lucindo fully cooperative and finding evidence against intentional performance enhancement, while noting the contamination could not be conclusively proven.

items.detail: Iasmin Lucindo lost to Amanda Lemos. Decision (Unanimous).

items.detail: Iasmin Lucindo defeated Angela Hill. Decision (Unanimous).

items.label: UFC 333 · vs. Nicolle Caliari
items.detail: Iasmin Lucindo is scheduled to face Nicolle Caliari at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi. Current record in the UFC 333 draft: 18-6-0, UFC 5-2-0.

items.label: Makes professional MMA debut
items.detail: Lucindo turned professional at only 14 years old after beginning kickboxing and MMA for self-defense. She has openly acknowledged how unusual that starting age was.

items.label: Receives camp mentorship from Amanda Nunes
items.detail: After Lucindo's UFC debut, former two-division champion Amanda Nunes visited her during training camp. Lucindo said the sessions gave her detailed lessons on fight IQ, professionalism and how a champion approaches preparation.

items.label: WIN · Sarah Frota · notable pre-UFC victory
items.detail: Before signing with the UFC, Lucindo defeated UFC veteran Sarah Frota, one of the strongest résumé markers from her regional career.

items.label: Starts karate in Curitiba
items.detail: Caliari says her father put her into karate so she would stay active and learn self-defense. Competition changed how she felt about it, and she began taking the sport seriously after early tournament success.

items.label: Moves from karate into Muay Thai
items.detail: After becoming a successful youth karate competitor, Caliari wanted a more physical full-contact sport. She began Muay Thai at 15 and later added jiu-jitsu as she moved toward MMA.

items.label: WIN · Morgana Silva · TKO R1
items.detail: Professional MMA debut at Imortal FC 2 in Curitiba. Caliari stopped Morgana de Cassia Silva with punches in the opening round. Record: 1-0.

items.label: LOSS · Syuri Kondo · unanimous decision
items.detail: Her second professional fight took her to Japan for Pancrase 279. Kondo won all three rounds on the judges' cards. The loss became an early checkpoint in Caliari's development, particularly in the wrestling and grappling parts of MMA. Record: 1-1.

items.label: WIN · Edna Oliveira Ajala · TKO R2
items.detail: Caliari returned in Brazil at Adventure Fighters Tournament 9 and stopped Edna Oliveira Ajala with punches late in the second round. Record: 2-1.

items.label: WIN · Thuany Fernandes · KO R1
items.detail: At Curitiba Top Fight 11, Caliari knocked out Thuany Valentim Fernandes with punches in the first round. Record: 3-1.

items.label: WIN · Itzel Esquivel · TKO R2
items.detail: Caliari made her LFA and U.S. debut in Houston, stopping Itzel Esquivel with punches in round two. This was her third straight stoppage win. Record: 4-1.

items.label: First roughly two-year layoff
items.detail: Caliari did not fight between November 2017 and October 2019. The UFC notes the layoff in her career history, but there is no reliable public source tying the entire gap to one specific injury.

items.label: LOSS · Kay Hansen · submission R3
items.detail: Caliari returned at Invicta FC 37 and was submitted by Kay Hansen with a guillotine choke in the third round. Record: 4-2.

items.label: Second roughly two-year layoff
items.detail: Another long gap followed the Hansen loss. Again, the inactivity is documented, but the available record does not establish one specific injury as the cause of the entire layoff.

items.label: WIN · Midian Fernandes · TKO R1
items.detail: Caliari returned at Face the Danger 23 and stopped Midian Fernandes Vicente with punches in the first round. Record: 5-2.

items.label: Third long period without a fight
items.detail: Caliari went nearly two more years before competing again. The UFC lists this as her third roughly two-year layoff. During this broader phase she was also teaching Muay Thai and working in gym management.

items.label: Moves from Curitiba to Florianópolis
items.detail: Caliari left Curitiba and relocated to Florianópolis to work with coach Márcio Malko at Thai Brasil Floripa. She has described it as a major career decision: she left her business and existing routine behind after Malko presented a plan aimed at getting her to the UFC.

items.label: WIN · Carolina Jimenez · armbar R2
items.detail: First fight after the long layoff and Florianópolis reset. Caliari submitted Carolina Jimenez with an armbar in the second round at Fight Music Show 3. Record: 6-2.

items.label: WIN · Daniella Antonelli · RNC R2
items.detail: Caliari followed the Jimenez win with another submission, choking out Daniella Antonelli in the second round. Record: 7-2.

items.label: WIN · Corinne Laframboise · armbar R1
items.detail: On Dana White's Contender Series, Caliari submitted Corinne Laframboise with an armbar at 4:45 of round one. The performance earned her a UFC contract. Record: 8-2.

items.label: LOSS · Ernesta Kareckaitė · split decision
items.detail: Caliari made her UFC debut at flyweight and lost a three-round split decision to Ernesta Kareckaitė. Record: 8-3, UFC 0-1.

items.label: LOSS · Carli Judice · TKO R3
items.detail: Carli Judice stopped Caliari with a knee to the body and punches at 1:30 of the third round at UFC 318. Record: 8-4, UFC 0-2.

items.label: Rebuilds her body for strawweight
items.detail: After competing at flyweight, Caliari committed to getting back to 115 pounds through a longer-term body-composition change rather than relying only on a fight-week cut. She had her breast implants removed as part of that plan, and later described a six-month process focused on reducing body mass for strawweight.

items.label: Injury cancels Carol Foro fight
items.detail: Caliari was originally scheduled to face Carol Foro in Seattle on March 28, 2026. UFC later reported that Caliari was injured and had to withdraw. The specific injury was not publicly identified in the source.

items.label: WIN · Shauna Bannon · arm-triangle R3
items.detail: Caliari made her UFC strawweight debut and submitted Shauna Bannon with an arm-triangle at 3:08 of the third round. It was her first UFC win and her fourth career submission. Record: 9-4, UFC 1-2.

items.label: Booked vs. Iasmin Lucindo · UFC 333
items.detail: Caliari is scheduled to face Iasmin Lucindo at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi. She enters the matchup 9-4 overall with all nine professional wins coming by stoppage.

items.label: Leaves law school in final year to choose fighting
items.detail: Caliari studied law but left during her final year when she felt forced to choose between school and fighting professionally. She has said her heart chose fighting.

items.label: Teaches women's Muay Thai and helps run gym business
items.detail: Alongside her own fighting career, Caliari taught Muay Thai classes for women through 2022 and handled administrative and operational work at the gym where she trained.
